title: 'Am I ready to trade?' daily psychological readiness self-test
description: Ch. 57's 5-question psychological readiness self-test (how do I feel physically / how did I trade yesterday / have I done my trade planning / how is my mood / how busy is my schedule), each scored 0/1/2, summed 0-10, color-coded per the book's own bands (<=4 red = don't trade, 5-6 yellow = trade cautiously, 7-8 green, 9-10 yellow again). Purely subjective, no market data, no provider calls -- the cheapest, most self-contained piece of ch. 57. Store one entry per calendar day. Scoped to just this self-test, not the broader 17-line market-context homework spreadsheet from the same chapter (that needs new/unavailable data sources and is a separate, larger idea).

checklist.step: Add a data model + endpoint(s) to record and retrieve a daily 5-question self-test score, one entry per calendar day (per user, if the app has any per-user concept -- otherwise one global entry per day, matching how the rest of this single-user app works).
Implement the book's own color-banding thresholds (<=4 red, 5-6 yellow, 7-8 green, 9-10 yellow) as a pure function over the summed score.

Decide whether 'how did I trade yesterday' auto-populates from yesterday's closed_trades realized P&L (a reasonable, cheap enhancement over Elder's own manual-recall version) or stays a fully manual input, and record the rationale.
Unit tests covering each score band boundary (4/5, 6/7, 8/9) and the auto-population behavior if implemented.

decisions.decision: 'How did I trade yesterday?' stays a fully manual score field on POST /api/daily-homework (yesterday_trading_score, still required, still 0/1/2, still the caller's own explicit answer). A separate read-only GET /api/daily-homework/yesterday-trading-suggestion endpoint offers a *suggested* value (2 for a net gain, 1 for exactly breakeven, 0 for a net loss, derived from the sum of closed_trades.realized_pnl for rows exited yesterday; null suggested_score/net_realized_pnl when nothing closed that day) that a form may use to pre-fill the field, but this app never writes yesterday_trading_score on the user's behalf.
decisions.rationale: Considered and rejected auto-computing yesterday_trading_score server-side and either (a) silently substituting it whenever the caller omits it, or (b) always overriding whatever the caller submits. Elder's own question is a subjective self-assessment ('how did I trade', not 'what was my P&L') -- a mechanical net-P&L read can't distinguish a profitable trade taken by breaking the trading plan from a small disciplined loss taken exactly on-stop, both of which a trader may reasonably want to score differently than the raw dollar sign alone implies. A separate suggestion endpoint gets the 'cheap enhancement over manual recall' benefit the task description calls out (the frontend form can pre-fill the field so most days require zero extra typing) without ever silently overriding the trader's own subjective judgment, and keeps the pure suggestion logic (app.portfolio.homework.suggested_yesterday_trading_score) independently testable from the persistence/upsert logic.

decisions.decision: One `daily_homework_entries` row per calendar day, keyed by `date` as the primary key (not a synthetic id). POST /api/daily-homework upserts: a second submission for a date that already has a recorded entry overwrites that day's five scores and recorded_at rather than rejecting with 409/422 or creating a second row, and always returns 201 either way -- mirroring POST /api/portfolio/positions' and POST /api/watchlist's identical 'same status code whether created or merged/no-op' convention. `date` is optional on the request, defaulting to today (server UTC date) if omitted, so a caller can also backfill/correct an earlier day's entry.
decisions.rationale: This is a single-user app (per CLAUDE.md/docs/Architecture.md's existing single-row-account/no-auth convention) with no per-user concept to key on, so 'one entry per calendar day' reduces to date-as-primary-key, the same pattern OHLCVCacheORM/ExtendedDataCacheORM already use for their own per-key uniqueness. Upsert-over-reject was chosen because Elder's own homework habit is a same-morning, possibly-redone task (re-scoring after further reflection, or correcting a mis-click) rather than an audit log that must preserve every historical submission attempt -- a 409 would just force the client to DELETE-then-POST for no real benefit, and total_score/band are pure computed fields anyway so there's no other data to reconcile from a prior submission the way, say, POST /api/portfolio/positions' quantity-merge has to.

decisions.decision: GET /api/daily-homework/today returns a wrapper object (`DailyHomeworkTodayResponse { entry: DailyHomeworkOut | null }`) rather than a nullable top-level response body, and never 404s when today's entry doesn't exist yet.
decisions.rationale: This codebase's existing convention for 'this might not be available yet' is a wrapper/sibling field that's null under a documented condition (IBKRScannerParamsResponse.categories gated by state, WatchlistItemOut.signal/confidence/confidence_band, BreadthResponse's unavailable_count) rather than the whole response body itself being absent or null -- keeping this endpoint consistent with that pattern, rather than introducing the only nullable-top-level-body response in the API, was preferred over the alternative of a raw `response_model=DailyHomeworkOut | None`. Not recording today's entry yet is the normal state for most of every day (before the trader has done the self-test that morning), not an error condition, so 404 (this codebase's convention for a genuinely missing/wrong-key resource, e.g. DELETE /api/watchlist/{ticker} for an unwatched ticker) would misrepresent it.

comments.summary: Blocking: suggested_yesterday_trading_score uses exact float equality (net_realized_pnl == 0) to detect a breakeven day. Binary floating point can't exactly represent most two-decimal currency sums, so a genuinely breakeven day across 2+ closed trades (e.g. sum([100.10, 5.05, -105.15]) == -1.15e-14) falls through to 'traded poorly' (0) instead of 'neutral' (1). The existing breakeven test only uses 50.0/-50.0, both exactly representable in binary floating point, so it doesn't catch this. Fix: round to cents or use math.isclose before the equality check.

Non-blocking: docs/architecture/Backend.md §7's persistence table enumeration wasn't updated to mention the new daily_homework_entries table (continuing a pre-existing staleness -- closed_trades/extended_data_cache are already missing from that sentence too). Tracked as a follow-up per precedent commit 5d5b86d.

Non-blocking: _today()/_utcnow() naive-UTC helpers are now duplicated a 4th time across app/api/routers/{portfolio,watchlist,homework}.py and app/data/cache.py rather than shared from one module. Pre-existing pattern this PR continues, not a new regression, but worth consolidating.

Verified record_daily_homework never calls suggested_yesterday_trading_score -- the 'stays manual' decision is genuinely reflected in code, not just in the decisions entry.
